prerequisites: Prior knowledge of kinematics and dynamics of rigid bodies and constrained systems.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the fundamental concepts of robot dynamics and hardware architecture.
Analyze the robotic system through its main functional subsystems (actuators, transmissions, etc.).
Formulate integrated mathematical models for the simulation of the robot within its operating environment.
Comprehend the dynamics of a robot and its components.
Construct models of varying levels of complexity, with the aim of developing predictive models with different degrees of accuracy.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: overview of robot topologies, open/closed kinematic chains, examples of serial/parallel manipulator architectures
Kinematics: transformation matrices, forward and inverse kinematics, differential kinematics
Static and kinematic analysis: kinetostatics, manipulability ellipsoids
Dynamics: modeling of robot dynamics, inverse dynamics, dynamics with simple control loops

Robot components: modeling and functional analysis of actuators (electric, fluidic), mechanical transmission elements (gears, belt drives, harmonic drives, etc.), end-effectors, modeling of actuator–transmission–robot systems
assessment_rules: Assessment will consist of a written examination aimed at evaluating the student’s knowledge of the course content and the ability to apply it to a case study. The final grade will be assigned based on the correctness, relevance, and completeness of the solutions provided.
